about: The HyperSVG conformance files (10.15) and what a reader gives for each. read: "ok" when the reader returns the files, or the code it refuses with. check: the error codes the checker gives on the files it returned, [] for none. maxBytes: the size limit the reader is given (dataBytesEach when absent). repack: unpacking and packing again gives the same bytes. pack: what the packer gives for a folder: the file it writes, or the code it refuses with.

cases.says: A valid asset: one scene, one drawing.
A valid asset whose scene places a component.
The same file read by a host whose limit is 1,024 bytes: over the limit.
The drawing was changed after packing; the digests were not made again.
A file inside the record was changed after packing; the digests were not made again.
The drawing was changed and every digest made again. The files are still valid, so it checks clean.
A script was put in the drawing and every digest made again. The digests match; the checker refuses it.
A control's target was renamed in scene.json and every digest made again. The checker refuses it.
A cleaner removed two paint attributes, then the host re-packed it. It checks clean.
A cleaner removed a part's data-hsvg-motion, then the host re-packed it. The digests match; the binding now moves a part past its range.
A file path with a .. segment.
An absolute file path.
A file path written with backslashes.
members lists a file that files does not hold.
files holds a file that members does not list.
A plain 2.0 drawing with no record.
The record line is not right after the <svg> start tag.
The record holds a key an asset cannot hold.
The record's format is not hsvg/2.0.
The drawing has a tool record of its own, made by hand. The packer never writes this, and the reader refuses it (2.13).
The one-scene asset's folder.
The component asset's folder.
A folder whose drawing already has a tool record: the packer refuses it.
